questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In electron spin resonance (ESR) dating, trapped electrons in crystal defects are measured non-destructively, commonly in which materials?
options: Not applicable to sedimentary materials at all in any circumstance whatsoever
Trapped electrons in crystal defects. Non-destructive. For tooth enamel, quartz
Destructive method requiring whole-sample dissolution and subsequent chemical analysis
Only for fresh igneous and volcanic minerals with a high uranium content in the rock
questions.solution: ESR: analog of luminescence. Detects trapped charge. Combined with U-series for teeth.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A thorough landslide hazard assessment must weigh which combination of geological and environmental factors?
options: The angle of the slope measured at a single point
Rainfall intensity recorded during the wet season
Vegetation cover density determined from satellite data
questions.solution: Landslide risk: combination of hazard (trigger), exposure (infrastructure), vulnerability. Multi-factor analysis required.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: P-T path determination from garnet zoning and inclusions:
options: Garnet core = early P-T. Rim = peak conditions. Inclusions record path
Garnet rims record the earliest conditions of metamorphism
Inclusions are younger than the host garnet and record late events
Only the bulk composition of the whole rock is ever required for the analysis
questions.solution: Garnet: chronometer. Inclusion assemblages at different distances from core = different P-T. Thermobarometry.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A migmatite rock is the product of which process of metamorphism?
options: Complete melting followed by magma crystallization
Shallow burial diagenesis of a sedimentary unit
Injection of an unrelated granitic intrusion
questions.solution: Migamatite: mixed rock (leucosome + melanosome). Represents partial melting at deep crustal levels. Transition to igneous.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the age, subdivision, and structural expression of the Delhi Supergroup?
options: Mesozoic (Triassic-Cretaceous) shelf sediments with rich marine ammonite faunas
Proterozoic (1.8-0.8 Ga). Alwar + Ajabgarh + Gogunda. Folded into Delhi fold belt
Archean (3.4-2.5 Ga) greenstone-granite terrain of the Bundelkhand craton block
Paleozoic (Cambrian-Permian) glacial and coal-bearing rift sequences of the Gondwana
questions.solution: Delhi: NE-SW trending fold belt. Marble, quartzite, schist. Built of Delhi (Red Fort).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A braided stream channel pattern typically indicates which conditions in the river?
options: High sediment load and variable discharge
Low gradient and stable low sediment load
Deep single channel cut into bedrock
questions.solution: Braided: multiple channels, high load, variable flow. Common in glacial outwash, arid regions, steep gradients.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: According to the Coulomb criterion, the shear strength of a rock is given by:
options: τ = c only, with no contribution from the normal stress or friction angle
τ = σ·tan(φ) only, assuming zero cohesion for every rock type
Coulomb criterion: τ = c + σ·tan(φ). c = cohesion, φ = friction angle
τ = σ always, independent of cohesion and the friction angle
questions.solution: Brittle: Hoek-Brown criterion. Rock joints: Barton-Bandis (JRC, JCS).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Ductile shear zones classified by their sense of offset record which kind of progressive displacement?
options: Uniform displacement with no strain gradient, since strain is identical in the walls and the centre
Progressive displacement. Normal, reverse, strike-slip. Strain gradient from wall to center
No displacement, the zone is simply a zone of static recrystallization
Brittle only, with discrete fracture surfaces and no ductile flow
questions.solution: Shear zones: mylonite series (S-C mylonite → ultramylonite → pseudotachylyte).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes a doline, the two ways it forms, and the form produced when dolines coalesce?
options: Point where groundwater emerges at the surface to form a stream of flowing water in the landscape
Natural underground void formed by the dissolution of limestone rock by water
Positive relief feature rising above the surrounding plain surface in the karst region
Closed depression. Solution vs collapse doline. Uvala: coalescing dolines
questions.solution: Doline: funnel-shaped. Polje: large flat-floored depression. Karst plain: lapies + dolines.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Arc basalts are generated by flux melting of the mantle wedge, which is evidenced by what trace-element signature?
options: Fluid from slab → mantle wedge melting. Hydrous → low F. High large-ion lithophile (LIL) / Nb-Ta negative anomaly
Decompression melting of upwelling asthenosphere beneath a mid-ocean ridge with no contribution from the subducting slab
MORB generated at a mid-ocean ridge with low water and high MgO content
Plume melting in the deep mantle with high ³He/⁴He and alkaline enrichment
questions.solution: Arc basalt: elevated Ba/La, low Nb/La. Subduction signature. Adakite: slab melting.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The Green-Ampt model of infiltration describes two stages: an initial high rate followed by:
options: Two-stage: initial (high rate) → steady state (f_c). Wetting front, suction head
A single constant rate of infiltration that continues throughout the entire duration of the storm
Darcy's law applied to the unsaturated zone at all times of the event
No wetting front ever develops during the infiltration process at the site
questions.solution: Green-Ampt: f = K_s·(1 + ψ·Δθ/F). F = cumulative infiltration. ψ = suction at wetting front.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How are the 14 Bravais lattices distributed among the seven crystal systems?
options: 6 types. Only primitive lattices, one for each crystal system, exist
32 types. Each point group generates its own distinct lattice type
Cubic (P, I, F), Tetragonal (P, I), Orthorhombic (P, C, I, F), Hexagonal (P), Trigonal (R), Monoclinic (P, C), Triclinic (P)
7 types. One lattice per crystal system: cubic P, tetragonal P, orthorhombic P, hexagonal P, trigonal P, monoclinic P and triclinic P
questions.solution: Bravais: 14 space lattices. Crystal systems: 7. Point groups: 32. Space groups: 230.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The fold shown in cross-section (beds sag downward about the axial plane) is a(n):
questions.solution: Downward-sagging limbs dipping toward the axis define a syncline (youngest beds in core).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Lower mantle minerals: bridgmanite (Mg,Fe)SiO₃:
options: Perovskite structure. Most abundant mineral in Earth by volume
Olivine structure. It dominates the mineralogy of the lower mantle
Garnet structure. Majorite garnet is the most abundant lower mantle mineral
Feldspar structure. Plagioclase persists stably throughout the lower mantle
questions.solution: Bridgmanite: perovskite structure. ~75% of lower mantle. Discovered in meteorite (Tenham).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Water draining from abandoned sulfide-bearing coal and metal mines, known as acid mine drainage, typically has a pH within what range?
questions.solution: AMD: sulfide minerals oxidize to produce sulfuric acid. pH can be <3. Devastating to aquatic ecosystems. Treatment expensive.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The magnetotelluric (MT) geophysical method makes use of which source of electromagnetic energy?
options: Acoustic waves produced by a surface source
Gravity data reduced for terrain and latitude
questions.solution: MT: uses natural EM fields (solar wind, lightning). Measures E and H at surface. Images subsurface resistivity.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A sequence boundary (SB) in stratigraphy represents which kind of surface?
options: Maximum flooding surface marking peak transgression
Transgressive surface of initial sea level rise
Condensed section of slow deep-water sedimentation
questions.solution: SB: erosion surface from subaerial exposure during sea-level fall. Separates sequences. Key sequence stratigraphy surface.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is chalk composed of, and what are its characteristic physical properties?
options: Coarse-grained limestone with abundant large shelly fossils throughout
Dolomitic limestone formed by magnesium replacement of calcium
Evaporite deposit of halite and gypsum from a restricted basin
questions.solution: Chalk: White Cliffs of Dover. Pure CaCO3. Used in cement, lime.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Pressure shadow mineral growth indicates:
options: Brittle fracturing under low confining pressure
Rapid crystallization from a cooling magma
questions.solution: Pressure shadows: fibrous mineral growth on rigid porphyroclast ends. Indicates ductile flow. Fibers track deformation path.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is a low-grade, large-tonnage copper deposit hosted by fracture-controlled sulfides in a porphyritic intrusion?
options: Sedimentary deposit formed by the evaporation of copper-rich brines in a closed lacustrine basin
Placer deposit enriched by stream transport of heavy copper minerals
High-grade veins confined to narrow fissures near a granite contact
Low-grade, large-tonnage. Fracture-controlled Cu-Fe sulfides in porphyritic intrusion
questions.solution: Porphyry Cu: stockwork veins. Chalcopyrite, bornite. Largest Cu source globally.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What do slickenlines on a fault surface indicate, and what do their steps reveal?
options: Planar mineral bands on the fault surface that record the age of the faulting event
Linear scratches on fault surface. Indicate slip direction. Steps show sense
Circular markings on joint surfaces produced by groundwater mineral precipitation
Curved striations that are always perpendicular to the direction of fault slip
questions.solution: Slickenlines: calcite/quartz fibers. Steps: Riedel shears. Sense from stepping direction.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Lithosphere-asthenosphere boundary (LAB):
options: 650 km depth. A sharp phase-change surface at the base of the mantle transition zone
Inner core. The boundary where solid iron begins to convect vigorously
Core-mantle boundary. A thermal boundary layer marked by ultra-low velocity zones and post-perovskite phase transitions
Rheological boundary. Mechanical lithosphere ~100 km (continental) to ~50 km (oceanic). Seismic low-velocity zone
questions.solution: LAB: seismic discontinuity. Thermal: ~1300°C isotherm. Electrical conductivity change.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which zones define the diagenetic environments from near-surface burial to uplift?
options: No distinct stages, with diagenesis occurring as one continuous unvarying process
Only burial-related diagenesis, with surface and uplift processes excluded entirely
Only uplift-related diagenesis, excluding near-surface and burial processes
questions.solution: Eogenesis: vadose/meteoric. Mesogenesis: compaction, cementation. Telogenesis: dissolution, fracturing.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which image processing technique merges high-resolution panchromatic data with lower-resolution multispectral data to sharpen detail?
options: Resampling the multispectral bands to a coarser resolution without any use of the panchromatic band
Applying high-pass filters to enhance edges for visual interpretation
Merge high-res panchromatic with low-res multispectral. Brovey, IHS, PCA, Gram-Schmidt
Classifying the image into thematic land cover categories
questions.solution: Pan-sharp: 0.3m pan + 1.2m MS → 0.3m MS. Spectral distortion vs spatial improvement tradeoff.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: According to the relative motion between adjoining plates, plate boundaries are classified into which categories?
options: Divergent boundaries only, since the convergent and transform margins are passive features of old ocean floors
Convergent margins alone, because all plate motion is accommodated by subduction beneath the continental crust
Divergent (mid-ocean ridge), Convergent (subduction, collision), Transform (conservative). Triple junctions
Transform faults only, as ridges and trenches mark ancient inactive boundaries within plates
questions.solution: Triple junctions: RRR (Afar), TTT (Japan), FFF (San Andreas). Hess (1962) — seafloor spreading.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In ophiolites, chromite occurs in which form and in which part of the mantle sequence?
options: Chromitite bodies forming only within stratiform layered intrusions, never in the mantle sections of ophiolites
Chromite concentrated only by residual lateritic weathering of peridotite outcrops
Podiform: mantle section. Stratiform: layered intrusion. Cr/(Cr+Al) indicates tectonic setting
Chromite composition giving no indication of the tectonic setting of formation
questions.solution: Podiform: mantle, harzburgite host. Stratiform: layered mafic intrusion. Cr#: higher = more depleted mantle.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the geological setting, age, and lithology of the Karewa Group of Kashmir?
options: Glacial till and moraines deposited by valley glaciers of the Kashmir Himalaya ranges
Pleistocene lake deposits in Kashmir. Fluvio-glacial. Loess interbeds. Blue clay
Aeolian dune sands that accumulated in a hot desert at the base of the Himalaya front
Marine shelf sediments with open-ocean foraminifera of the Tethyan seaway deposits
questions.solution: Karewa: 1500m thick. Plant fossils, pollen. Paleoclimate archive. Saffron cultivation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: LiDAR return types: first return = canopy top. Last return =:
options: Tree canopy top surface before penetration
Atmospheric scattering layer above the canopy
questions.solution: LiDAR: multiple returns. First = top. Last = ground (if penetrates canopy). Bare earth model.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes an inselberg and the specific names given to its granite and other forms?
options: Landform produced by the erosive action of moving glacier ice over bedrock
Isolated bedrock hill in arid/semiarid plains. Bornhardt (granite), kopje
Sediment body deposited where a river enters a lake or sea and spreads out
Island of land formed in the middle of a river channel by sediment deposition during floods
questions.solution: Inselberg: weathering remnant. Pediment: gently sloping bedrock surface around inselberg.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the hardness value of quartz on the Mohs scale of mineral hardness?
questions.solution: Quartz (SiO2) — hardness 7. Scratches glass. Common in all rock types.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How do the minerals corundum and spinel differ from each other in thin section?
options: Both minerals are isotropic and therefore show identical relief and no birefringence
Corundum: high relief, hexagonal, extreme birefringence. Spinel: cubic, isotropic
Same appearance with no distinguishing optical properties
Both are hexagonal with strong pleochroism in plane light
questions.solution: Corundum: n=1.762-1.770, δ=0.008. Spinel: n=1.712-1.736, isotropic.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which chemical formula correctly represents the composition of the mineral quartz?
questions.solution: Quartz is silicon dioxide, SiO₂, one of the commonest minerals.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What wavelengths of ultraviolet light are used to test fluorescence in minerals?
options: Short-wave (254nm) vs long-wave (366nm). Calcite, fluorite, willemite fluoresce
All minerals fluoresce equally brightly under both short-wave (254nm) and long-wave UV light
Fluorescence is observed only when minerals are heated
No mineral fluoresces because luminescence needs radioisotopes
questions.solution: Fluorite: blue (SW). Calcite: red, pink. Willemite: green (SW). Used in mineral identification.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the chemical formula and structural type of muscovite, a mica group mineral?
options: Trioctahedral phyllosilicate with three octahedral cations
Framework silicate belonging to the feldspar group
Tectosilicate with a three-dimensional SiO4 framework
questions.solution: Muscovite: white mica. Dioctahedral (2 Al per formula unit). Common in granite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How do the braided outwash channels of glacial periods differ from the meandering floodplain rivers of interglacials?
options: Glacial (braided, outwash) vs interglacial (meandering, floodplain). MIS stages shift patterns
River patterns remain exactly the same throughout all climatic stages of the Quaternary period
Rivers show only glacial braided patterns in every climatic stage of the stratigraphic record
Rivers show only interglacial meandering patterns in every climatic stage of the stratigraphic record of the region concerned
questions.solution: Climate: wet/dry cycles shift sediment load. Terrace formation during transitions.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which characteristic of a material, its reflectance plotted against wavelength, allows the material to be distinguished by remote sensing?
options: Reflectance vs wavelength. Different materials have unique signatures
The reflectance is constant across all wavelengths, for every material type
Identical spectral signatures for all of the minerals and the rocks that are present
Random reflectance values, which cannot be measured with any degree of certainty at all
questions.solution: Vegetation: high NIR reflectance. Water: low reflectance. Minerals: absorption features at specific wavelengths.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In what ground conditions are steel sets typically used as tunnel support?
options: Light shotcrete cover applied only to the crown of the tunnel
Rib supports (I-beams) in weak ground. Wood blocking between steel and rock
No support of any kind is needed once the weak ground is fully exposed
Light timber lagging and steel lattice girders placed only on the tunnel invert
questions.solution: Steel sets: used in heavy squeezing/loose ground. Lattice girders. Forepoling.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is an amorphous volcanic glass with no crystals and conchoidal fracture?
options: Volcanic glass (amorphous, no crystals). Conchoidal fracture
Pegmatitic rock with exceptionally large crystals of quartz and feldspar
Porphyritic rock with phenocrysts in a fine-grained groundmass
Coarse-grained plutonic rock with interlocking equant minerals
questions.solution: Obsidian: rapid cooling of felsic lava. Used for tools by ancient humans.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is considered the cause and scale of the Permian-Triassic mass extinction about 252 million years ago?
options: Triassic-Jurassic event linked to the breakup of Pangaea and CAMP volcanism
End-Ordovician extinction caused by the Hirnantian glaciation and sea level fall
Largest extinction (96% species). Siberian Traps. Ocean anoxia. H2S
K-Pg event caused by the Chicxulub asteroid impact with an iridium anomaly
questions.solution: P-Tr: 'Great Dying'. Volcanic CO2 → warming → anoxia. Terrestrial: fungi spike.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What distinguishes clastic from non-clastic (chemical or biochemical) sedimentary rocks?
options: Clastic: chemical precipitation from seawater. Non-clastic: transported rock fragments
Clastic: chemical/biochemical precipitation. Non-clastic: fragments of older rocks
Clastic: fragments of pre-existing rocks. Non-clastic: chemical/biochemical precipitation
Both types are composed of transported fragments of pre-existing rocks with no chemical input
questions.solution: Clastic: conglomerate, sandstone, shale. Non-clastic: limestone, evaporite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Amphibolite, the medium-to-high-grade equivalent of basalt or gabbro, consists mainly of which minerals?
options: Chlorite + epidote + albite + actinolite. Low-grade equivalent of basalt
Hornblende + plagioclase. Medium-high grade. Equivalent to basalt/gabbro
Pyroxene + garnet + feldspar. High-grade anhydrous equivalent of basalt
Glaucophane + lawsonite + jadeite. High-pressure equivalent of basalt
questions.solution: Amphibolite: medium to high grade (amphibolite facies). No pyroxene (granulite has pyroxene).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In groundwater geophysics, the nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) method is notable because it can do what?
options: Seismic refraction profiles used for mapping the depth to the top of the bedrock
Resistivity sounding curves interpreted as a one dimensional layered earth model of the subsurface geology
Nuclear magnetic resonance (MRS). Direct detection of groundwater. T₂* decay time for pore size
Gravity gradient survey used for locating deep seated basement density contrasts
questions.solution: MRS: surface NMR. Water content ε, decay T₂*. Logging NMR also. Porosity + permeability estimate.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An ore body of 2 Mt has an average metal grade of 1%. The contained metal is about:
questions.solution: Metal = tonnage × grade = 2 Mt × 1% = 20 thousand tonnes (kt).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A rock retains 50% of its original parent isotope (half-life 0.7 Gyr). Its radiometric age is about:
options: 0.7 Gyr (equal to one full half-life of the parent)

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How is the plunge of a fold hinge line defined relative to the horizontal?
options: Angle between the fold limbs measured perpendicular to the hinge line
Angle of fold hinge line from horizontal
The dip angle of the axial plane measured normal to the hinge
The compass bearing of the hinge line measured from true north
questions.solution: Plunging fold: hinge line inclined. Non-plunging: horizontal hinge.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 4% moisture, 25% volatile matter and 8% ash. Its fixed carbon is:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A slug test involves an instantaneous change in water level and is most suitable for:
options: Pumping at a constant rate for several continuous days at the pumping well site
A long term test of the aquifer that lasts for many months of continuous pumping
Instantaneous change in water level. For low K aquifers. Hvorslev, Bouwer-Rice
Steady pumping to equilibrium flow conditions in an observation well of the aquifer under test
questions.solution: Slug test: quick, inexpensive. T estimate for monitoring wells. Near-well conditions.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the hardness value of feldspar on the Mohs scale of mineral hardness?
questions.solution: Feldspar — hardness 6. Most abundant mineral group in Earth's crust.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes a knickpoint in the longitudinal profile of a river and what it indicates?
options: Longitudinal profile that is perfectly smooth with no breaks in gradient along its entire length from source to mouth of the river
Break in river longitudinal profile (waterfall, rapids). Indicates rejuvenation or lithological control
Sediment body deposited where a river enters a lake or sea and spreads out over the bed of the basin floor
Longitudinal profile with a perfectly uniform slope from the source to the mouth of the river channel throughout the whole of its course
questions.solution: Knickpoint: upstream migration by headward erosion. Base level change indicator.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which spaceborne sensor acquires 36 bands at 250-1000 m resolution with a 1-2 day revisit for global monitoring?
options: Nine spectral bands at 30m spatial resolution with a sixteen-day revisit period
36 bands, 250-1000m. 1-2 day revisit. 2330km swath. Global monitoring
Thirteen bands at 10m spatial resolution with a 5-day revisit period
A single panchromatic band with sub-metre spatial resolution
questions.solution: MODIS: Terra (AM) + Aqua (PM). NDVI, SST, fire, snow cover, land cover. Daily global.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What does Coulomb's earth pressure theory account for that Rankine's does not?
options: Considers wall friction and sloping backfill. Wedge analysis
Considers only smooth vertical walls with horizontal backfill
Ignores friction and assumes zero wall roughness entirely
Is valid only for cohesive soils with no internal friction
questions.solution: Coulomb: wedge trial. Wall friction δ reduces active pressure. P_a = ½γH²K_a.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What coarse-grained texture, with crystals visible to the eye, is typical of plutonic rocks?
options: Glassy texture formed by extremely rapid cooling of lava
Porphyritic texture with phenocrysts in a fine groundmass
Fine-grained texture in which individual minerals are invisible
questions.solution: Phaneritic: crystals >1mm. Slow cooling at depth.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which rock units are separated by the Great Unconformity exposed in the Grand Canyon?
options: Mesozoic limestone resting directly on Paleozoic sandstone across the canyon
No unconformity exists; the entire section is one continuous sequence
Archean granite basement overlain by Proterozoic quartzites in the canyon
Proterozoic Vishnu Schist overlain by Cambrian Tapeats Sandstone
questions.solution: Great Unconformity: ~1.2 Ga gap. Vishnu (1.7 Ga) → Tapeats (525 Ma). Angular + nonconformity.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In sedimentary geology, what does the provenance of a sediment refer to?
options: The mechanism of sediment transport from source to the basin of deposition
Source area of sediments (composition, age, tectonic setting)
The environment in which sediments are deposited and later lithified into rock
Post-depositional changes including compaction, cementation and dissolution of sediment
questions.solution: Provenance: heavy mineral analysis, zircon U-Pb dating, paleocurrents.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which mineral pair is the essential assemblage of the eclogite facies at very high pressure?
options: Garnet + omphacite. Very high P. Densest crustal rock (~3.5 g/cm³)
Amphibole-bearing assemblage that is stable at moderate pressures
Low-density quartz-feldspar rock formed at very shallow crustal depths
Hydrous mineral assemblage stable in shallow crustal levels
questions.solution: Eclogite: subduction zone. Coesite in UHP rocks. Diamond-grade: >4 GPa.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Potential field data: upward continuation:
options: Transforms the anomaly to a lower elevation, sharpening the shallow source signatures
Removes the regional gradient without any change to the depth content of the data
Transforms anomaly from measurement height to higher elevation. Enhances deep sources
Increases the noise floor while leaving the anomaly amplitude completely unchanged
questions.solution: Upward continuation: low-pass filter. Deeper sources preserved, shallow attenuated.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Unconformity-related uranium deposits, like those in the Athabasca Basin, are characterized by what features?
options: Placer accumulation of heavy radioactive minerals in mature beach sands
Sandstone-hosted roll-front uranium precipitated along redox boundaries between oxidized and reduced aquifer zones
Volcanic-hosted uranium associated with peralkaline rhyolite calderas
Athabasca Basin (Canada). High grade (>1% U₃O₈). Basement + sandstone. U/Pb age ~1.5 Ga
questions.solution: Unconformity: massive U within altered basement. Cigar Lake, McArthur River.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A mineral has passed through 1 half-life of an isotope whose half-life is 5.73 (in the given time units). Its age is:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the proximate analysis of coal, fixed carbon is obtained by subtracting from 100% the sum of:
options: Carbon, hydrogen and oxygen determined by ultimate analysis
Volatile matter and sulphur percentages only
questions.solution: Fixed carbon (%) = 100 − (moisture + volatile matter + ash) in proximate analysis.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The aluminium silicate mineral andalusite crystallizes in which crystal system?
questions.solution: Andalusite (Al2SiO5) — prismatic, square cross-section. Chiastolite variety has cross pattern.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which term describes obtaining information about the Earth's surface without physical contact, from satellites or aircraft?
options: Direct physical sampling of Earth materials by geologists working in the field and laboratory
Acquiring information about Earth without physical contact (satellite, aircraft)
Borehole drilling and coring to recover subsurface rock core samples
Seismic surveys using artificial energy sources generated at the surface
questions.solution: RS: electromagnetic radiation interaction with Earth surface. Passive (solar) and active (radar).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What fine-grained texture (<1 mm), typical of volcanic rocks, has crystals too small to see?
options: Glassy texture produced by sudden chilling of a lava surface
Coarse-grained texture in which crystals are visible to the naked eye
Porphyritic texture with large crystals in a fine groundmass
questions.solution: Aphanitic: crystals not visible. Rapid cooling at surface.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is coal composed of, and what rank series does it follow from peat to anthracite?
options: Chemical precipitate formed by direct evaporation of organic-rich brine
Organic sedimentary rock (plant remains). Rank: peat→lignite→bituminous→anthracite
Metamorphic rock formed by recrystallization of pre-existing limestone at high temperature and pressure
Igneous rock formed by cooling of organic-rich magma at the Earth's surface
questions.solution: Coal: swamp environments. Peat (low rank) → Anthracite (high rank, high C).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What term describes a fracture in rock along which displacement has occurred, and what do hanging wall and footwall refer to?
options: A fracture with no displacement across which the rock layers remain perfectly matched
Fracture with displacement. Hanging wall (above) vs footwall (below)
A fracture along which the two sides have moved relative to each other, always vertically
A fold in which the layers bend without breaking and maintain their continuity
questions.solution: Hanging wall: block above fault plane. Footwall: block below.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What streak colour does the mineral magnetite produce when rubbed on a streak plate?
questions.solution: Magnetite (Fe3O4) — strongly magnetic. Black streak. Important iron ore.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the vesicular mafic volcanic rock that is darker and denser than pumice?
options: Coarse-grained plutonic rock composed of plagioclase and pyroxene
Granitic rock with interlocking quartz, feldspar and mica crystals
Vesicular mafic volcanic rock (darker, denser than pumice)
Felsic glass that is less dense and floats on water
questions.solution: Scoria: basalt with vesicles. Cinder cones. Heavier than pumice.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 10% moisture, 20% volatile matter and 10% ash. Its fixed carbon is:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the purpose of a Geotechnical Baseline Report (GBR)?
options: A legal document used only to sue the contractor after completion
A construction method statement prepared by the main contractor
Defines baseline ground conditions for contractual purposes
An optional report that is never used in contract administration
questions.solution: GBR: contractual baseline. Used in dispute resolution. FIDIC conditions of contract.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Correlation of coal seams from one borehole to another is done using which methods?
options: Only the lithological similarity of adjacent seams in the boreholes
Only geophysical logging of the borehole sections is employed
Facies analysis, palynology, geochemistry, geophysical logging
Only the matching of seam thickness between neighbouring boreholes
questions.solution: Correlation: palynomorph assemblages, geochemical fingerprinting, well logs (density, gamma ray).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What does seismic microzonation map at a detailed local scale?
options: Regional mapping at national scale that ignores local site amplification and liquefaction
Detailed hazard mapping. Amplification, liquefaction, landslide susceptibility
Site-specific mapping that is carried out only at a single building location
Broad-scale national zoning maps used only for general planning purposes
questions.solution: Microzonation: 1:10,000 scale. For urban planning and building codes. Site-specific response analysis.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which SAR imaging mode transmits and receives multiple polarizations, such as HH, HV, VH, and VV, to characterize targets?
options: A single polarization channel used only for basic target detection applications
Dual polarization acquisitions only, never collecting full quad-polarimetric data
Single polarization data that ignores all phase information entirely
Multiple polarization channels (HH, HV, VH, VV). Target characterization
questions.solution: PolSAR: decomposition (Pauli, Freeman-Durden). Crop classification, soil moisture.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Uniaxial compressive strength (UCS) testing: intact rock sample. Granite UCS typically:
questions.solution: Granite: 100-250 MPa. Sandstone: 20-170 MPa. Shale: 5-25 MPa. Basalt: 100-300 MPa.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the Theis equation for unsteady flow, drawdown s is expressed as s = Q·W(u)/(4πT), where the dimensionless parameter u equals:
options: s = Q·t/T giving a straight line on arithmetic paper
s = Q·W(u)/(4πT). u = r²S/(4Tt). W(u) = well function
s = Q·ln(r)/T for steady radial flow to the well
s = Q/(4πT) evaluated at a fixed distance from the well
questions.solution: Theis: non-equilibrium. Type curve matching for T and S estimation. Jacob approximation for small u.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The groundwater modeling code MODFLOW solves three-dimensional flow using which numerical method?
options: Analytical solutions for steady flow to a single well
A finite-element method on an unstructured mesh grid
A Monte Carlo approach to solve the flow equations
questions.solution: MODFLOW: USGS code. Block-centered finite difference. Grid cells. Steady or transient.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Under which conditions do kink bands typically form in strongly foliated rocks?
options: Strongly foliated rocks under compressive stress parallel to foliation
Isotropic massive rocks under equal hydrostatic confining pressure applied in all directions
Unfoliated coarse-grained plutonic rocks subjected to low-grade retrograde metamorphism
Homogeneous rocks deformed by pure tension acting normal to the future fold axial plane
questions.solution: Kink bands: angular folds in well-foliated rocks. Foliation rotates sharply across kink band.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What type of solid solution series do plagioclase feldspars form between albite and anorthite?
options: Only the albite end-member exists naturally in plutonic rock-forming mineral suites
Only the anorthite end-member crystallizes from magmas
K-spar series with continuous K-Na substitution only
Albite (Na) to Anorthite (Ca) — continuous solid solution

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Porosity n is the ratio of void volume to total volume; secondary porosity, in contrast to primary intergranular porosity, arises from:
options: The ratio of the solid volume of the rock to the total void volume that is present within the rock
Void volume/total volume. Primary (intergranular) vs secondary (fracture, solution)
The ratio of the total volume of the rock to the volume of the voids that are present within the rock
The ratio of the solid volume of the rock to the volume of the voids that are present within it
questions.solution: Porosity: sand 25-40%, sandstone 5-30%, granite <1%. Effective porosity: interconnected pores.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What are the secondary fractures R, R′, P, T and Y in a strike-slip shear zone collectively called, and what do they indicate?
options: Only a single set of shear fractures develops, oriented parallel to the zone boundary
Riedel shears are random fractures that carry no information about the shear sense
R, R', P, T, Y shears in strike-slip zone. Indicate shear sense
The R' shear is synthetic and always lies at about 15° to the shear zone boundary

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A bed dipping at 30° shows a width of 10 m across a horizontal surface. Its true (perpendicular) thickness is about:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is shotcrete and how is it applied in underground construction?
options: Concrete cast in timber formwork and cured for twenty-eight days before any loading
Precast panels bolted onto the rock face with no bonding material at all
Sprayed concrete (dry or wet mix). Steel fiber reinforced. Applied to rock surface
Poured tremie concrete placed underwater through a tremie delivery pipe
questions.solution: Shotcrete: immediate support. Add accelerator. Wire mesh or fiber. 50-100mm thick.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquifer (K = 10 m/day) of cross-section 100 m² has a hydraulic gradient of 0.02. The groundwater discharge is about:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which structural feature describes linear fabric elements such as mineral alignment, intersection or stretching in rocks?
options: A planar fabric element defined by the preferred orientation of platy minerals
A surface of fracture with no measurable displacement, dividing the rock into blocks
Linear fabric element (mineral alignment, intersection, stretching)
A large-scale fold structure formed by regional horizontal compressive stress
questions.solution: Lineation: parallel to fold axes, mineral elongation, or intersection of foliations.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the geological nature of the Indo-Gangetic Plain and its sedimentary fill?
options: Rocky terrain composed of exposed Precambrian basement of the Indian Shield
Basement exposed at surface with no sediment cover anywhere in the plain
Thin sedimentary cover resting directly upon the Deccan volcanic pile
Foredeep basin. Thick alluvium (Tertiary-Quaternary). Aquifer system

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the faulted block shown, the hanging wall has moved up over the footwall. This is a:
options: Normal fault produced by extensional tectonic stress
Detachment fault with low-angle listric geometry
Strike-slip fault with dominantly horizontal displacement
questions.solution: Hanging wall up = reverse fault, caused by compression.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Competent vs incompetent layers in folding:
options: Competent layers are thinnest at the fold hinges and thickest on the fold limbs
Competent layers buckle and are thicker at hinges. Incompetent flow into hinges
Both layer types deform identically, so no thickness variation develops anywhere
Incompetent layers remain rigid and unchanged while competent layers thicken on the limbs
questions.solution: Competent: quartzite, sandstone. Incompetent: shale, salt. Parasitic folds in incompetent layers.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which plutonic rock has roughly equal plagioclase and alkali feldspar with little or no quartz?
options: Plagioclase ≈ alkali feldspar. Little or no quartz
Ultramafic plutonic rock composed almost entirely of olivine and pyroxene
Mafic rock dominated by calcic plagioclase, augite and minor olivine
Quartz-rich granite with alkali feldspar greatly exceeding plagioclase
questions.solution: Monzonite: intermediate between diorite and syenite. Plag=K-spar.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Quartz (hardness 7) will scratch, but not be scratched by, which mineral?
options: Topaz with a hardness of 8 on the Mohs scale
Corundum which is harder than topaz (9)
questions.solution: A mineral scratches anything softer; quartz (7) scratches feldspar (6) but not topaz/corundum/diamond.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What process and climatic conditions lead to the formation of laterite and bauxite?
options: Dry climate with intense mechanical weathering and no chemical alteration
Periglacial freeze-thaw cycles producing frost-shattered angular debris
Intense chemical weathering under tropical monsoon. Fe/Al enrichment. Bauxite
Cold climate with glacial grinding and slow chemical weathering of the bedrock
questions.solution: Laterite: duricrust. Age: Tertiary-Quaternary. Transition: laterite → bauxite (Al-rich).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The general three-dimensional groundwater flow equation reduces to Laplace's equation under which condition?
options: Darcy's law applied only to horizontal flow, with no variation in head or velocity across space
Steady state conditions require that the storage term in the groundwater flow equation be zero
Transient groundwater flow ignores the storage term and assumes a constant hydraulic conductivity everywhere

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In coastal aquifers, the depth of the freshwater-saltwater interface below sea level is given by the Ghyben-Herzberg relation as:
options: Freshwater-saltwater interface. Ghyben-Herzberg: z = 40·h (h = head above sea level)
z = 80h giving an interface depth that is twice the Ghyben-Herzberg value of the site area
z = 20h giving an interface depth that is half the Ghyben-Herzberg value
z = h meaning the interface lies at exactly the same depth as the measured head value above sea level
questions.solution: Ghyben-Herzberg: z = ρ_f·h/(ρ_s-ρ_f). For ρ_s/ρ_f = 1.025: z ≈ 40h.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Tunnel boring machine (TBM) selection depends on:
options: Only the uniaxial compressive strength of the intact rock material
Only the amount of water inflow expected in the tunnel heading
Only the abrasiveness of the rock as measured by the CAI index
Rock mass strength, abrasivity, discontinuities, water inflow
questions.solution: TBM: hard rock (open), soft ground (shielded), mixed face (hybrid). CAI abrasivity index important.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which ultramafic, potassic rock is the primary source rock for diamonds?
options: Felsic volcanic rock rich in quartz that forms continental flood provinces
Ultramafic potassic rock. Source rock for diamonds
Mafic volcanic rock composed of plagioclase, pyroxene and magnetite
Granitic plutonic rock consisting of quartz, muscovite and alkali feldspar
questions.solution: Kimberlite: diamond-bearing. Pipe-like bodies. South Africa, Siberia.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A symplectite is best described as what type of texture in metamorphic rocks?
options: Regular growth of a single mineral phase in optical continuity across a twin plane with no second phase present
Overgrowth of a new mineral in crystallographic continuity around an older detrital or igneous core
Intergrowth of two minerals (e.g., Cpx + Pl) replacing higher-P assemblage. Opx + Cpx + Pl from Grt breakdown
Exsolution of a second mineral phase from a homogeneous alkali-feldspar host during slow cooling
questions.solution: Symplectite: vermicular texture. Decompression reaction. Fingerprint of rapid exhumation.

questions.stem: How does X-ray diffraction identify clay minerals using glycol treatment and potassium saturation?
options: Ethylene glycol treatment expands smectite. K-saturation collapses vermiculite
No treatment is required because all clay minerals give unique and distinctive XRD patterns
Heat treatment alone destroys the 7Å peak of all smectites
Acid treatment removes interlayer water from kaolinite only
questions.solution: Smectite: expands with glycol (d₀₀₁ 17Å). Illite: no change (10Å). Kaolinite: disappears with K-sat.
